Private DNS seems like a reasonable solution but it has its own problems.

Search engines are definitely a big hurdle. Unless web crawlers perform their duties at a lower layer of the internet than I imagine (ie, scanning public IP ranges for content rather than mapping sites listed on DNS server), any site hosted on an alternative DNS will not appear in a search engine that doesn't also map that DNS.

Worse, even if you had a search engine checking alternative DNS providers, the client would still need to be configured with a matching DNS server or the name of the host won't resolve properly.

That wouldn't be a problem if this theoretical alternative search engine returned domains as IP addresses but it also raises the problem of requiring direct IP access to a domain. I personally tried extracting voat's public IP as a registrar-proof access method, but it turns out that cloud flare blocks direct IP access. So there's another thing that you would have to resolve.
